items.excerpt: A University of Manchester study found AI chatbots can match or even exceed human responders at providing emotional support, especially for anger and fear. The decisive factor was not warmth but 'specific, actionable guidance' rather than generic reassurance.

Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology researchers gave robots a curiosity-driven learning signal and found they picked up language roughly twice as fast as incurious counterparts. The robots spontaneously played and reproduced the same characteristic grammatical errors human toddlers make before recovering from them.

Tohoku University unveiled an AI-powered closed-loop framework that couples machine learning to automated experiments so predictions are continuously refined by real lab feedback. The team says the self-driving-lab approach could shorten clean-energy materials development by years.

IIT Gandhinagar physicists used machine learning to sweep the huge parameter space of extended Higgs theories and narrow it to the configurations still allowed by collider data. The surviving scenarios include a possible lighter Higgs sibling near 82 GeV, giving experimentalists a concrete place to look.

Penn Engineers released PeptiVerse, an open-source AI platform that forecasts the chemical and biological properties of peptides before anyone synthesizes them. Screening in silico first could cut the cost and time of developing peptide drugs such as weight-loss therapeutics.

NSF NCAR researchers are building AI emulators such as CAMulator to attack the notoriously hard two-to-six-week 'subseasonal' forecast gap. CAMulator can generate 480 simulated years per day, roughly 350 times faster than the physics model CAM6 it learned from.

New work shows membership-inference attacks can pull sensitive patient information out of medical AI models far more effectively than the field assumed. The leakage is concentrated among underrepresented patient groups, meaning the privacy cost falls hardest on the people models already serve worst.

MIT CSAIL's SceneSmith uses three collaborating AI agents to author realistic 3D indoor scenes for robot training, packing in far more objects than prior generators. The synthetic playgrounds let robots rehearse everyday manipulation before ever touching a real room.

In MIT's four-week JARVIS Challenge, student teams designed, built and test-fired a working jet engine with AI copilots at their side. The verdict: AI can substantially accelerate safety-critical hardware engineering, but human engineering judgment was still the decisive differentiator between teams.

MIT Media Lab researchers propose 'neural transparency' — surfacing a model's internal activation patterns to ordinary users while they are still designing a personalized chatbot. The goal is to let people anticipate a system's behavioral risks at design time instead of discovering them after deployment.

A 'double neural bypass' brain-computer interface restored both movement and the sensation of touch to a man paralyzed since a 2020 diving accident, by stimulating brain and spinal cord together. Keith Thomas, the trial participant, had wanted one thing above all: to feel his dog again.

Most U.S. hospitals still monitor clinical AI with governance frameworks built for static, pre-LLM software, leaving silent model drift undetected. The authors argue responsibility for continuous evaluation belongs with senior leadership, not the IT department.

OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol produced a proof of the cycle double cover conjecture, a graph-theory problem open for more than 50 years. Mathematicians say the result shows AI tools are already changing how mathematical research gets done, not just how it gets checked.

Neural networks trained to detect biosignatures in Earth-based chemistry can be spoofed by unfamiliar molecular patterns, confidently labeling non-living samples as alive with 100% confidence. The finding is a warning for astrobiology missions that plan to lean on AI classifiers to flag life beyond Earth.

IonQ and QuantumBasel report that a hybrid quantum-classical model matched selected classical methods on a machine-learning task while its energy use grew only linearly with qubit count. They project a crossover against GPU simulation near 34 qubits, though the result covers a single workload and quantum inference only.

Creativity researcher Scott Barry Kaufman shows that prompting a language model to 'be maximally creative' makes its output more predictable, not more original. His argument: models trained to predict statistically common patterns are structurally biased against the statistical rarity that defines original ideas.

Where recommendation algorithms reinforce what people already believe, a new study tests a dialogic AI chatbot deliberately built to challenge assumptions and surface competing viewpoints. Students who used it reasoned more deeply and were more willing to revise their initial positions on contested topics.

Google Research offers a mathematical account of why diffusion models produce genuinely new images rather than copies: a 'score smoothing' effect that emerges from neural-network training. The models interpolate between training examples along a hidden data manifold instead of memorizing them.

Google Research ran a national-scale study of SymptomAI, a conversational agent for everyday symptom assessment, with 13,917 participants. Clinicians preferred SymptomAI's differential diagnosis over that of other clinicians in more than half of cases.

University of Illinois researchers found the brain starts committing to a decision far earlier than assumed, with higher regions feeding rapid top-down signals back into primary sensory cortex. The feedback-loop architecture is a template engineers could borrow for future AI systems built less like feedforward stacks.
